title: Win-loss
description: A review on every closed deal: why it was won or lost, with the reasons from your own taxonomy, confirmed by the rep and approved by a manager. When a deal closes, Canon drafts its review with AI from the deal's calls, meetings and notes, on the owner's ChatGPT plan, keeping only quotes it finds word for word. Reviews open as deals close, or by backfill. Admins keep the reasons, the program's settings and the competitors you meet.

ai.prompt:
You draft a win-loss review of one closed deal for the rep who owned it to confirm. Read the deal and every call, meeting and note on it, then say why the deal was won or lost.

- summary: three sentences at most, in plain words: what the buyer chose and why, as the record shows it.
- drivers: two to five reasons from the reasons list, the one that decided it as weight "primary" (exactly one) and the rest "contributing". For each: direction "negative" if it hurt us, "positive" if it helped; strength "strong" when the buyer said it decided or nearly decided the deal, else "normal"; and one to three quotes, each copied word for word from a call's transcript, a meeting's notes or a note, with that record's id, its kind (call, meeting or note), its date as YYYY-MM-DD and the speaker when the transcript names one. A reason you can't quote, leave out.
- competitor: the key of the competitor the buyer chose or compared us with, from the competitors list, or leave it out.

Write nothing the record doesn't say. If the record is too thin to explain the outcome, return a summary that says so and no drivers.
